nodes.name: Package substrate & interposer
nodes.description: The multi-layer organic substrate and silicon/organic interposer that form the structural and electrical backbone of a 2.5D AI accelerator package. Carries the logic die, HBM stacks, power delivery, thermal vias, and signal routing from the die to the board-level connector. The substrate-interposer stack includes build-up layers, resin systems, copper traces, vias, and thermal management features—all facing acute capacity and material constraints in 2025–2026.
nodes.notes: 2025–2026 bottleneck: substrate + interposer assembly is a critical chokepoint in AI accelerator volume ramps due to capacity constraints at TSMC CoWoS, material shortages (T-glass, ABF), and long tool lead times (18–24 months).

nodes.name: Organic substrate base structure
nodes.description: Multi-layer organic laminate (6–14+ layers for high-density AI accelerator packages) composed of resin matrix (BT or ABF) with embedded glass fiber cloth (T-glass or E-glass) and copper foil. Forms the foundation carrying signal routing, power planes, and mechanical support for the interposer and die assembly.
nodes.notes: Material bottleneck: T-glass (91% supply from Nittobo) faces 10–20% shortage through mid-2027; BT resin and ABF film similarly constrained.

nodes.name: Silicon interposer with RDL
nodes.description: Silicon interposer (2.5D package core) carrying Redistribution Layer (RDL) that routes signals between the logic die, HBM stacks, and substrate. Typically 300–500 µm thick, with deep trench capacitors and low-impedance interconnects. TSMC CoWoS-S is the volume architecture; Samsung iCube is secondary.

metrics.name: TSMC CoWoS-S capacity 2026
metrics.description: TSMC monthly CoWoS capacity expanding from ~75k wafers/month in early 2025 to 110–130k wafers/month by end of 2026 per CEO guidance. CoWoS sold out through 2025 and into 2026.

metrics.name: TSMC CoWoS market share 2025
metrics.description: TSMC holds ~60% of global 2.5D/3D stacking advanced packaging market; CoWoS-S and I-Cube (silicon interposer 2.5D) are volume architectures for AI accelerators.

metrics.name: Top-3 customer allocation of TSMC CoWoS 2026
metrics.description: Major customers (NVIDIA, AMD, hyperscalers) have locked >85% of TSMC's total CoWoS production capacity, leaving <15% for second-tier AI chip makers, ASIC vendors, startups.

nodes.name: ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film)
nodes.description: Dielectric build-up film used in high-density IC substrates, composed of resin-impregnated fine glass fibers (50–100 µm thickness per layer). ABF is the premium segment for advanced AI accelerator packages, enabling tight trace spacing and high layer count.

metrics.name: ABF market growth CAGR 2021–2028
metrics.description: ABF demand CAGR 20.73% from 2021 to 2028, driven by 5G, AI, and EV; Film Type B (premium ABF) accounts for 31.4% revenue share in 2025.

metrics.name: Ajinomoto ABF capacity increase 2025
metrics.description: Ajinomoto's new Gunma facility completed March 2025 and reached full operations October 2025, increasing ABF capacity by ~50% to 2030.

metrics.name: Ajinomoto ABF price increase 2026
metrics.description: Ajinomoto announced 30% price increase for core ABF laminated film, effective Q3 2026, citing strong demand and tight supply.

nodes.notes: Ajinomoto holds dominant market share for ABF; expansion capacity through 2030; additional Gifu site planned for 2032 startup.

nodes.name: BT resin laminate substrate
nodes.description: Bismaleimide-Triazine resin laminate produced by Mitsubishi Gas Chemical and competing suppliers. Lower-cost alternative to ABF for mid-range packages; less common in leading-edge AI accelerators but used in secondary packages and thermal management layers.

metrics.name: BT substrate price hike 2025
metrics.description: BT substrate and fiberglass prices eye ~20% hike mid-2025 amid AI boom and supply shortage.

nodes.notes: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical owns key BT resin formula; high Tg, moisture resistance, low DK/DF suitable for power-dense packages.

nodes.name: T-glass (Boron-free glass fiber cloth)
nodes.description: High-performance glass fiber cloth with reduced coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE), critical for substrates carrying high-power, high-frequency signals in AI accelerators. T-glass dominates AI substrate designs; supply is heavily concentrated at Nittobo (91% global market share).

metrics.name: Nittobo T-glass global market share 2025
metrics.description: Nittobo dominates certified T-glass production; ~91% global market share + 60–70% NER-glass market share.

metrics.name: T-glass supply shortage 2026
metrics.description: Taiwan IC substrate makers forecast 10–20% supply gap of T-glass material in 2026; demand doubled entering 2025–2026.

metrics.name: Nittobo T-glass capacity expansion target 2027
metrics.description: Nittobo plans to triple T-glass capacity by 2027; new equipment online expected mid-2027 at earliest.

metrics.name: Nittobo price increase August 2025
metrics.description: Nittobo raised prices across glass fiber product line by 20% in August 2025; planned another 20–30% increase for April 2026.

nodes.notes: Critical bottleneck: Nittobo near-monopoly (91% share) with constrained capacity through mid-2027. New capacity expected only from 2027; new equipment requires 6 months to stabilize yield.

nodes.name: Copper trace routing and signal redistribution
nodes.description: Multi-layer copper trace patterning, via drilling, plating, and controlled impedance routing across substrate and interposer layers. Enables signal integrity for high-speed interfaces (HBM, chiplet links).

nodes.name: Thermal via filling and copper column formation
nodes.description: Electroplating and copper paste filling of thermal vias (50–200 µm diameter) to conduct waste heat from the die to the substrate backside. High via density required in AI packages (700W+/module); copper filling is energy-intensive and equipment-limited.

metrics.name: Substrate tool lead time expansion 2024–2025
metrics.description: Equipment lead times extend up to 18–24 months for substrate expansion projects; CCL makers and substrate suppliers face significant delays in new capacity buildout.

nodes.notes: Bottleneck: electroplating and via-fill equipment capacity becomes gated by specialized tool suppliers (ASMPT, Kulicke & Soffa). New equipment takes 18–24 months to procure and integrate.

nodes.name: Power delivery network (PDN) in substrate
nodes.description: Embedded power planes, decoupling capacitors (eMIM, MIM), and integrated inductors within the substrate to deliver clean, stable power to the logic die at 700W+ power dissipation. PDN target impedance < 1 mΩ at core frequencies. Co-designed with silicon.
nodes.notes: Advanced PDN techniques (eMIM-T, CoaxMIL) embed passive devices in substrate for impedance optimization; co-design with silicon is critical.

nodes.name: Kinsus Interconnect Technology Corp.
nodes.description: Taiwan-based IC substrate and PCB manufacturer. Leading supplier of BT and ABF substrates for AI accelerators; strong volume growth in 2024–2025. Publicly traded (listed as TPE: 3189).

metrics.name: Kinsus 2025 revenue growth
metrics.description: Kinsus recorded strongest performance with 2025 annual revenue surging 28.87% driven by AI substrate demand.

metrics.name: Kinsus ABF substrate market segment
metrics.description: Kinsus leads in volume production of BT substrates for consumer electronics; growing ABF segment for AI. Revenue share estimate 8–15% of total substrate market (most conservative basis).

nodes.notes: Growth driver: AI substrate demand. Capacity expansion ongoing with client subsidies and pre-payments.

nodes.name: Unimicron Technology Corp.
nodes.description: Taiwan-based IC substrate manufacturer. Market leader in ABF substrates; 15.2% revenue share in 2024 package substrates market. Primary supplier to major AI accelerator makers; aggressive expansion into high-end ABF for server/AI applications.

metrics.name: Unimicron IC substrate revenue share 2024
metrics.description: Unimicron leads sector with 15.2% revenue share in 2024 package substrates market overall; top revenue leader.

metrics.name: ABF substrate market leader position 2025
metrics.description: Unimicron makes the most ABF and has the biggest share; none of top five exceeded 18% individual share in 2025.

nodes.notes: Historical bottleneck: 2021–22 ABF shortage drove record earnings for Unimicron. Expansion of ABF capacity for AI demand continuing.

nodes.name: Ajinomoto Fine-Techno Co., Ltd.
nodes.description: Japanese subsidiary of Ajinomoto Group. Sole/dominant producer of ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film), the premium dielectric material for high-density IC substrates. Controls majority of ABF supply globally; critical supplier to all AI accelerator makers.

metrics.name: Ajinomoto ABF global supply dominance
metrics.description: Ajinomoto holds dominant/monopoly share of ABF supply; Film Type B (premium ABF) accounts for 31.4% of total ABF revenue in 2025.

metrics.name: Ajinomoto ABF sales growth 2025
metrics.description: ABF sales for high-performance boards used in AI servers and networks increased 28% for full year FY2025.

metrics.name: Ajinomoto ABF expansion capex 2025–2030
metrics.description: Ajinomoto committed JPY 25 billion in capex for ABF production expansion; new facility in Gunma completed March 2025, full ops October 2025, capacity increase ~50%.

metrics.name: Ajinomoto Gunma facility capacity increase
metrics.description: New Gunma varnish production facility reached full-scale operations October 2025, increasing total ABF capacity by ~50% toward 2030.

metrics.name: Ajinomoto future site (Gifu)
metrics.description: Ajinomoto acquired land in Gifu May 2026; construction scheduled 2028, operations targeted 2032 to support demand from 2030 onwards.

nodes.notes: Critical bottleneck: Ajinomoto's ABF capacity and expansion roadmap gate AI accelerator substrate volume through 2028. Announced 30% price increase effective Q3 2026.

nodes.name: Nittobo Chemical Industries, Ltd.
nodes.description: Japanese glass fiber manufacturer. Dominates certified T-glass (boron-free) production, the critical substrate base material for AI accelerators. Holds ~91% global T-glass market share; sole practical source for leading-edge substrates.

metrics.name: Nittobo T-glass global market share 2025
metrics.description: Nittobo dominates certified T-glass production globally; approximately 91% market share + 60–70% NER-glass share.

metrics.name: Nittobo T-glass capacity constraint 2026
metrics.description: Taiwan IC substrate makers forecast 10–20% supply gap of T-glass in 2026; Nittobo constrained through mid-2027.

metrics.name: Nittobo T-glass capacity expansion target
metrics.description: Nittobo announced August 2025 plan to triple T-glass capacity during 2026–2027; investment >¥50 billion in Japan and Taiwan.

metrics.name: Nittobo Fukushima plant expansion investment
metrics.description: Nittobo investing ¥15 billion ($96 million) to expand T-glass capacity by up to threefold at Fukushima production base; facilities online in 2027.

metrics.name: Nittobo price increase August 2025
metrics.description: Nittobo raised prices across glass fiber product line 20% in August 2025; planned another 20–30% increase for April 2026.

metrics.name: Nittobo new capacity commissioning timeline
metrics.description: Newly installed glass fiber equipment typically requires ~6 months to reach stable yield; meaningful relief not before mid-2027.

nodes.notes: CRITICAL BOTTLENECK: Nittobo's 91% T-glass share and constrained capacity (10–20% shortage through mid-2027) gates AI accelerator substrate volume. Partnership with Nan Ya to handle 20% by 2027; plans next-gen T-glass by 2028.

nodes.name: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company, Inc.
nodes.description: Japanese chemical company. Owns key BT resin formula and manufacturing technology patents; supplier of bismaleimide-triazine (BT) resin laminates for IC substrates. Competes with Ajinomoto in substrate resin market.

metrics.name: BT resin market position
metrics.description: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company owns key material BT resin formula and manufacturing technology patents; high Tg, moisture resistance, low DK/DF.

nodes.notes: Key supplier of BT resin systems; competing against Ajinomoto ABF for design wins in AI substrate market.

nodes.name: Nan Ya Printed Circuit Board Corp.
nodes.description: Taiwan-based PCB and IC substrate manufacturer. Secondary player in ABF substrates; also partnering with Nittobo on T-glass supply chain to expand capacity. Strong in BT substrates.

metrics.name: Nan Ya PCB substrate market position 2024
metrics.description: Nan Ya PCB is among top-5 global substrate makers; ~10% market share estimate in package substrates.

metrics.name: Nan Ya partnership with Nittobo T-glass
metrics.description: Nan Ya partnered with Nittobo to handle 20% of T-glass supply by 2027 as expansion effort.

nodes.notes: Strategic partnership with Nittobo to supplement T-glass supply; secondary player in high-end ABF but growing capacity.

edges.claim: AI accelerator module requires substrate and interposer as structural and electrical foundation.
Substrate-interposer module requires organic substrate base as structural foundation.
2.5D substrate-interposer stack requires silicon interposer with RDL for die-to-HBM signal routing.
Substrate must integrate power delivery network (PDN) to distribute 700W+ power to logic die at <1 mΩ impedance.
High-density substrate requires ABF dielectric layers for tight trace spacing and advanced designs.
Substrate requires T-glass (boron-free glass fiber) for low CTE and thermal stability in high-power packages.
Multi-layer substrate requires copper trace patterning and via formation for signal integrity.
High-power packages (700W+) require dense thermal vias filled with copper for heat dissipation.
Ajinomoto Fine-Techno is the dominant producer of ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film) globally.
Kinsus is a leading supplier of BT and ABF substrates for AI accelerators.
Unimicron is the market leader in ABF substrates with 15.2% revenue share in 2024.
Nan Ya PCB is a secondary player in ABF substrates with partnership on T-glass supply.
Nittobo is the dominant manufacturer of certified T-glass with ~91% global market share.
Mitsubishi Gas Chemical owns the BT resin formula and is a key supplier of BT laminates.
TSMC manufactures silicon interposers for CoWoS-S 2.5D packages; holds 60% global advanced packaging market share.

evidence.title: TSMC CoWoS Capacity Expansion: 75k to 130k Wafers/Month by 2026
evidence.summary: TSMC CEO C.C. Wei stated CoWoS capacity is 'sold out through 2025 and into 2026.' NVIDIA CEO Jenson Huang confirmed CoWoS assembly capacity is 'oversubscribed through at least mid-2026.' TSMC plans to expand monthly CoWoS capacity from 75,000–80,000 wafers today to 110,000–130,000 by end of 2026. Major customers have locked >85% of TSMC's total CoWoS capacity, leaving <15% for second-tier vendors.

evidence.title: Samsung iCube and SAINT 2.5D/3D Packaging Technology
evidence.sourceName: ASME International / Electronic Device Failure Analysis Society
evidence.summary: Samsung employs iCube 2.5D packaging technology and plans to unveil SAINT (Samsung Advanced Interconnection Technology) for 3D chip packaging. Samsung is secondary interposer supplier competing with TSMC CoWoS.

evidence.title: Ajinomoto Q4 FY2025 Earnings: ABF Structural Growth, 28% Sales Increase
evidence.summary: Ajinomoto reported ABF sales growth of 28% for full year FY2025 (ended March 2025), driven by surging AI server demand. New Gunma facility completed March 2025, reached full ops October 2025, increasing ABF capacity by ~50%. Company stated it has enough ABF capacity through 2030; announced 30% price increase effective Q3 2026.

evidence.title: Ajinomoto JPY 25B ABF Expansion Capex Plan Through 2030
evidence.summary: Ajinomoto announced JPY 25 billion (USD ~166M) capex investment by 2030 to boost ABF production capacity by 50%. New Gunma facility operational in October 2025. Gifu facility land acquired May 2026; construction 2028, operations 2032.

evidence.title: Ajinomoto Q4 2025 Sees Record Performance, ABF Capacity Through 2030
evidence.summary: Ajinomoto reported record earnings in Q4 FY2025; ABF for high-performance AI boards grew strongly. Company reaffirmed commitment to support demand through 2030 and into early next decade.

evidence.title: Nittobo T-Glass Shortage: 10–20% Supply Gap 2026, 91% Market Share Monopoly
evidence.summary: Taiwan IC substrate makers forecast 10–20% supply gap of T-glass material in 2026. Nittobo dominates certified T-glass production globally with ~91% market share. Demand has effectively doubled entering 2025–2026 driven by AI infrastructure. Capacity constraints not expected to ease until mid-2027.

evidence.title: Nittobo Triple T-Glass Capacity by 2027; 2028 Next-Gen Product; Nan Ya Partnership
evidence.summary: Nittobo announced plan to triple T-glass capacity during 2026–2027. Investing ¥50+ billion in Japan and Taiwan. Capacity expected 10–20% higher in FY2026 vs. current; double in FY2027. New equipment requires ~6 months to reach stable yield; meaningful relief not before mid-2027. Partnership with Nan Ya to handle 20% by 2027. Plans 2028 next-gen T-glass product.

evidence.title: Nittobo Raises Glass Fiber Prices 20% (Aug 2025), Plans 20–30% Increase (Apr 2026)
evidence.summary: Nittobo raised prices across glass fiber product line by 20% in August 2025. Company plans another price increase of roughly 20–30% effective April 2026, citing strong AI demand and tight supply.

evidence.title: Kinsus 2025 Annual Revenue Surge 28.87% Driven by AI Substrate Demand
evidence.summary: Kinsus recorded strongest performance with 2025 annual revenue surging 28.87% driven by AI substrate demand. Kinsus is a leading supplier of BT and ABF substrates for AI accelerators.

evidence.title: IC Substrate Leaders: Unimicron (15.2%), Kinsus, Nan Ya Market Share 2024–2025
evidence.summary: Unimicron leads IC substrate market with 15.2% revenue share in 2024 package substrates market. Top five players hold ~74% market share; none exceed 18% individually. Kinsus, Nan Ya, Unimicron posted double-digit revenue growth in 2024.

evidence.title: Unimicron Market Leader in ABF Substrates 2025; 2021–22 Shortage Drove Record Earnings
evidence.summary: Unimicron is the market leader in ABF substrates, making the most with the biggest share. Top five ABF suppliers hold ~74% market share. None of the top five exceeded 18% individual share in 2025. Historical context: 2021–22 ABF shortage drove record earnings for Unimicron.

evidence.title: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical: BT Resin Laminate for IC Substrates
evidence.summary: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company owns the key BT resin formula and manufacturing technology patents. BT resin has advantages: high Tg, high heat resistance, moisture resistance, low DK, low DF. Key supplier of BT resin laminates for IC substrates competing with Ajinomoto ABF.

evidence.title: Nan Ya Plastics Partnerships with Nittobo: 20% T-Glass Supply by 2027
evidence.summary: Nittobo and Nan Ya Plastics partnered to expand glass-fiber output. Nan Ya to handle 20% of T-glass supply by 2027 as part of capacity expansion effort to meet AI surge demand.

evidence.title: Substrate Expansion Equipment Lead Time: 18–24 Months, CCL Capacity Delays 2025
evidence.summary: Equipment lead times extend up to 18–24 months for substrate expansion projects. CCL makers launching new wave of advanced capacity expansion; equipment lead times create bottleneck. Substrate suppliers struggling to catch up with demand from AI-overbooked advanced packaging lines.
